subject: Onboarding metrics & billing definitions for MVP MAP
summary: Commercial MAP discussion with FastRetail to align milestone metrics, commit ramp schedule, and contract economics (true-ups, price protection, usage definitions). Procurement returned redlines; Redwood agrees to provide example true-up calc, a 30-day trial credit, and a drafted MAP that ties commit milestones to pricing collars.
messages:
From: Emma Lowe <emma@fastretail.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial ask: onboarding metrics, billing defs, and MAP timeline

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the caching notes you shared. Before we lock in the pilot MAP, our procurement and legal folks asked for clarification on three things that will directly affect our economics:

1) Definitions of "usage" for billing: do you bill purely by tokens, or do embeddings / reranking / cached KV hits count differently? We have a mix of real-time inference and heavy prefix reuse; we'd like to understand how that will map to committed units vs burst.

2) True-up cadence and calculation: procurement wants examples of how a quarterly true-up would work if our actual consumption exceeds commits, and whether there are waterfalls for overage pricing.

3) Price protection / collars: FastRetail needs a 12-month protection window on unit pricing as we ramp; if there are escalators, we need to see how they apply.

Attached: FastRetail_RFP_Specs.pdf (high-level usage patterns). Our short timeline — we need a committed baseline by 2027-01-10 to lock pricing for Q1. Can you share a draft MAP + SOW that maps milestones (pilot acceptance, 30-day production trial, commit go-live) to pricing?

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Lowe
Head of Product Partnerships
FastRetail

[Attachment: FastRetail_RFP_Specs.pdf]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lowe <emma@fastretail.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: onboarding metrics, billing defs, and MAP timeline

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. I copied Lauren (Sales Ops) and Karthik (Comms/Contracts) so we can capture redlines correctly. Short answers up-front and I attached a MAP draft and SOW skeleton: MAP_Draft_20261129.pdf, SOW_v1.pdf.

- Usage definitions: Redwood bills generation and embedding units separately; tokens are the default for generation. We also offer a "cached hit" discount when prefix/KV cache returns a hit — those are treated as 10% of standard token units for billing purposes (we'll show this in the SOW examples).

- True-up: typical cadence is quarterly with a waterfall: committed baseline -> 1x overage at commit rate -> >1.5x moves to higher overage band. We can provide a sample calculation.

- Price protection: we can offer a 12-month price lock on unit rates from contract signature; we typically allow a small annual escalator for infra costs (we'll propose a cap).

Next steps: please have procurement/legal send their redlines to me and we'll turn around a marked-up MAP by EOD Tuesday. If you can confirm the pilot acceptance criteria (latency < 250ms p90, test prompt set pass rate >= 95%), we'll map the milestones to the pricing ramps.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director of Sales, Redwood Inference

[Attachments: MAP_Draft_20261129.pdf, SOW_v1.pdf]

From: Procurement Team <procure@fastretail.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Lowe <emma@fastretail.ai>, Legal Team <legal@fastretail.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: FastRetail: redlines on MAP and economics (FR_Legal_Redlines_20261130.docx)

Vivek — attaching our redlines. High-level items:

- True-up frequency: we prefer semi-annual true-ups to reduce admin churn. If your standard is quarterly we will need a concession on the overage multiplier.

- Usage definition: we require explicit buckets for (a) interactive generation (token-based), (b) embeddings (per embedding unit), (c) KV/prefix cache hits (should not be charged at full token rate). We also want a clause addressing cached replication: if cache reduces downstream compute, we expect a proportionate billing credit.

- Price protection: we request a 12-month fixed unit rate with an annual cap of no more than 3% thereafter. We also ask for a one-time true-up grace in the first 90 days post go-live.

- Ramp: commit ramp must include a minimum baseline for Q1 (number provided in the redline). Failure to hit ramp can trigger a moderated true-up vs refund mechanism.

Please review edits and provide counter-language for the billing table and the true-up example.

Regards,
FastRetail Procurement

[Attachment: FR_Legal_Redlines_20261130.docx]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Lowe <emma@fastretail.ai>, Procurement Team <procure@fastretail.ai>, Legal Team <legal@fastretail.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FastRetail: redlines on MAP and economics (draft response)

Team — forwarding procurement redlines. Below is proposed counter-language I plan to send to FastRetail tomorrow unless you flag edits. Key points:

1) True-up cadence: agree to semi-annual true-ups (every 6 months) for this enterprise pilot, with illustrative calculation in the SOW. Overage multipliers will be 1.0x up to 120% of commit, 1.3x for 120-200%, and 1.8x beyond 200%. We should spell out an example where commit=1M units, actual=1.5M units => amount due calculation.

2) Usage buckets: accept explicit buckets in the billing table: generation (token-units), embeddings (unit-per-embedding), and cache-hit credit (10% of token rate). We'll include a definition for "cached hit" and a sampling audit process to validate metrics.

3) Price protection: offer 12-month price lock from signature + capped annual increase at 3% thereafter. For the first 90 days post go-live, offer a one-time true-up grace where we prorate overages to the first billing period.

4) Ramp mechanics: propose a staircase commit schedule tied to MAP milestones: Pilot Acceptance -> 60% commit -> 100% commit by 2027-03-01. Missed ramp triggers a remediation path (credits or refund mechanics) instead of immediate chargebacks.

Questions for Legal: is the 1.8x top band acceptable from a litigation/risk standpoint? Karthik, can you confirm if the audit process language for cache credits needs to live in the SOW or a separate measurement appendix?

I'll draft the marked MAP with these changes and circulate the MAP_Final_20261205.pdf for signature.

Thanks,
Vivek

[Planned attachment in next email: MAP_Final_20261205.pdf]

From: Emma Lowe <emma@fastretail.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@fastretail.ai>, Legal Team <legal@fastretail.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FastRetail: redlines on MAP and economics (follow-up)

Vivek — thanks for the quick counter. A few clarifications before we can accept:

- The example true-up calculation would be helpful in the SOW; please show a numeric example (commit=1,000,000 token-units; actual=1,500,000).
- For the cache-credit audit, FastRetail needs a lightweight verification: monthly sample logs and a one-time onboarding audit. If that adds scope, we can accept it in the SOW.
- The 3% cap on annual increases is acceptable; we need that in the main contract, not a side letter.
- Regarding ramp: we must lock the baseline no later than 2027-01-10 to hold Q1 pricing. Can Redwood provide a 30-day trial credit or usage cap for initial production testing?

If you can send the sample calc and the MAP with the proposed payment waterfall, procurement will do a final pass.

Best,
Emma

[Procurement/Legal are ready to turn around redlines within 24 hours when they see the sample calculation]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lowe <emma@fastretail.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procure@fastretail.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FastRetail: redlines on MAP and economics (final MAP + examples)

Emma — appreciate the clear asks. Attached is MAP_Final_20261205.pdf with:

- A worked true-up example: commit=1,000,000 token-units; actual=1,500,000 => calculation shows charges: 1,000,000 at commit rate, 500,000 at 1.3x overage (per agreed band) => line-item math.
- Billing table with explicit buckets (generation tokens, embeddings per-unit, cache-hit credit at 10%) and a short appendix describing measurement and monthly sample logs. Audit will be monthly samples + one onboarding audit.
- Price protection clause: 12 months firm from signature; thereafter capped annual increase at 3% (in main contract).
- Ramp schedule in MAP: Pilot Acceptance target 2027-01-15; 60% commit by 2027-02-01; 100% commit by 2027-03-01. We agree to the 30-day trial credit (one-time $X credit applied to first invoice) and a 90-day first-period true-up grace that prorates over the initial billing period.

Next steps: I will send the DocuSign envelope for the MAP + SOW after you confirm the $X trial credit amount is acceptable (we can make it a usage cap if you prefer). Once signed, procurement can run final redlines in 24 hours per your note.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/FR-2026-ONRAMP-ENVELOPE

Vivek Kulkarni
Director of Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

[Attachment: MAP_Final_20261205.pdf]
